_comment: Open abdominal steps, shared by laparotomy, open appendicectomy and open hernia repair.

step.abd.midline.title: Midline laparotomy incision
step.abd.midline.why: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.
how: Incise through skin, fat and linea alba, staying in the midline: drifting off it bleeds and weakens the closure.
Enter the peritoneum between forceps under direct vision, then extend with fingers protecting the bowel.
Extend as far as the operation needs. An inadequate incision causes more harm than a long one.
structuresAtRisk: Bowel adherent to the undersurface of a previous midline scar
Bladder at the lower end of a lower midline incision
pitfalls: A short incision that forces retraction injury on the liver and spleen.

step.abd.exploration.title: Systematic exploration
step.abd.exploration.why: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out. A systematic sequence is the only way to be sure the second pathology was looked for rather than merely not seen.
how: Follow the same sequence every time: liver and gallbladder, stomach and duodenum, spleen, small bowel from duodenojejunal flexure to caecum, colon and rectum, pelvis, retroperitoneum, hernial orifices from inside.
Run the small bowel hand over hand, both surfaces, in one direction.
Record what was normal as well as what was abnormal.
structuresAtRisk: Spleen, from retraction on the greater curve
Serosal tears from handling distended bowel
pitfalls: Stopping the exploration when the expected pathology is found.
Missing a second perforation because the first explained the free fluid.

step.abd.bowel-handling.title: Handling and assessing bowel
step.abd.bowel-handling.why: Bowel handled roughly becomes ileus, adhesions and, at the extreme, a serosal tear that becomes a leak.
how: Handle with the whole hand and moist packs; grasp the mesentery, not the bowel wall.
Assess viability by colour, peristalsis, mesenteric pulsation and bleeding from a cut edge, and re-assess after warm packs and time.
When viability is genuinely uncertain in an unstable patient, resect, leave discontinuous and plan a second look.
pitfalls: Deciding viability in the first 30 seconds.
Anastomosing bowel of doubtful perfusion to avoid a stoma.

step.abd.lavage.title: Peritoneal toilet
step.abd.lavage.why: Removing contamination is part of source control, but lavage does not substitute for closing the hole that produced it.
how: Remove particulate contamination mechanically from all four quadrants and the pelvis.
Irrigate with warm saline and aspirate it completely; fluid left behind is a collection.
Do not add antiseptic or antibiotic to the irrigation as a substitute for source control.
pitfalls: Lavage of a compartment that has not been fully opened, so the subphrenic collection is missed.
Leaving irrigation fluid in the abdomen.

step.abd.drain.title: Drain placement
step.abd.drain.why: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see. It does not prevent a collection and it does not rescue an anastomosis.
how: Place a drain when you want early warning of a specific complication, or to drain an established collection.
Bring it out through a separate stab wound in clean skin, secure it, and record the type and site in the note.
Decide in advance what output would change management, and hand that number over.
pitfalls: A drain placed 'just in case', which then becomes a route for infection.
A drain not recorded in the operative note.

step.abd.mass-closure.title: Mass closure of the abdominal wall
step.abd.mass-closure.why: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.
how: Use a continuous slowly-absorbable suture with a suture length to wound length ratio of at least four to one.
Take small bites close to the edge rather than large bites far from it.
Keep the bowel protected by an instrument or the assistant's hand for every single bite.
Do not close under tension. If the abdomen will not close, do not force it - manage it open.
structuresAtRisk: Small bowel caught in a closure bite
pitfalls: Large bites taken quickly at the end of a long case.
Closing an abdomen that is developing compartment syndrome.

step.abd.stoma.title: Stoma formation
step.abd.stoma.why: A badly sited stoma is a lifelong problem for the patient and a daily one for the stoma nurse. Siting is decided before the patient lies down, whenever there is time.
how: Site away from the costal margin, the umbilicus, the belt line, scars and skin creases, through the rectus muscle, where the patient can see it.
Bring out a tension-free, well-perfused segment; check the colour after the abdomen is closed.
Evert and mature a spouted ileostomy; a colostomy may be flush.
structuresAtRisk: Marginal vessels of the bowel being brought out
Inferior epigastric vessels at the trephine
pitfalls: Siting the stoma under a skin fold that is only apparent when the patient sits up.
A stoma under tension because the mesentery was not mobilised.
